title: Adaptive Cross-Layer INT8 Scale Scheduler and Microkernel Integration for Runtime SmoothQuant Support
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Implement an adaptive cross-layer scale scheduler and lightweight microkernel hooks to run activation-aware INT8 (SmoothQuant-like) profiles in production. This ticket covers the pipeline pieces needed to generate per-layer scale schedules from calibration runs, expose a compact runtime representation, and integrate microkernel selection + fallback policy so the serving runtime can apply activation rescaling with minimal latency overhead.
acceptance_criteria: Calibration pipeline emits compact per-layer scale schedules (<= 2KB/model) compatible with runtime loader
Serving runtime can apply rescale schedules inline with KV-cache and batching with <2ms p99 extra latency on 1k token requests for target models
Automated validation shows <= 0.6% average perplexity regression vs FP16 on internal eval suite for GLM/T5-family models after INT8 rescale application
Fallback path triggers automatically and maintains correctness when microkernel not available for a hardware+model combination
design_notes: Represent scale schedules as a versioned protobuf that maps layer-id -> {weight_scale, activation_scale, op_hint}
Scheduler should optionally merge adjacent layers with near-identical scales to reduce size and runtime branching
Microkernel interface: provide 3 hooks - pre-forward rescale, post-forward restore, and fused op with quantized GEMM when available
Fallback policy: runtime tries fastest microkernel, if missing or error then apply CPU/GPU generic shims with telemetry and degrade gracefully
implementation_notes: Calibration: extend existing per-workload calibrator to output 'scale-graph' and an attachable manifest
Runtime loader: add a new route in model metadata to fetch scale-schedules; cache keyed by model+version+schedule-hash
Kernel registry: extend kernel selector to consider 'rescale-fused' capability; fallthrough path applies elementwise multiply kernels
Telemetry: record per-request scale-application time, fallback counts, and quality drift signals for Optimize alerts
experiments: Ran offline calibration on redwood/llama-7B-int8-sim: compared three merge thresholds (0.01, 0.05, 0.1). Size dropped from 6.4KB to 1.2KB at 0.05 with negligible perf impact
Microkernel perf test on A100 vs T4: fused rescale+GEMM achieved 1.12x throughput on A100 and 1.05x on T4 for batch sizes 1-8 compared to generic path
Stress test with KV-cache heavy traffic (100 concurrent sessions): p99 tail increased by 1.6ms when applying rescale as separate ops; fused microkernel eliminated most of that overhead
perf_results: LLAMA-7B validation set: FP16 perplexity 12.8, INT8 w/ rescale 12.9 (+0.78%)
T5-large summarization: ROUGE-L delta -0.3 points between FP16 and INT8 w/ rescale across 500 examples
End-to-end latency: baseline 85ms p50 / 180ms p99; with fused kernel 88ms p50 / 182ms p99; with generic rescale 90ms p50 / 201ms p99
risks: Quantization profiles may overfit to calibration prompts; need diverse prompt sets to avoid quality regressions
Missing microkernel support across older hardware may increase fallback rates and cost
Merging compressed schedules could introduce subtle correctness bugs if layer mapping changes across model revisions
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Internal evaluation only - add opt-in config in staging for selected models and hardware
Phase 2: Canary on dedicated clusters with low-traffic customers; monitoring alerts for quality/regression
Phase 3: Gradual ramp to hosted API with automatic fallback and opt-out flag per-customer
Phase 4: Promote to default for models that pass regression gates for two weeks
qa_steps: Unit tests for loader and manifest parsing (edge cases: missing layers, partial schedules)
Integration test: model load -> calibration schedule applied -> sample outputs compared to golden FP16 baseline
Fuzz injection: corrupt schedule payloads to validate fallback behavior
A/B validation: compare user-visible quality metrics on held-out traffic during canary
